proposals.new_text:
---
title: "Why do I know exactly what I should do with my money — and still not do it?"
pubDate: "2026-08-14"
description: "Joel explores the gap between financial knowledge and financial action, drawing on behavioural economics research and the specific pattern he sees in clients who earn well but feel stuck."
slug: "why-do-i-know-exactly-what-i-should-do-with-my-money-and-still-not-do-it"
author: "Joel"
---

Most people who come to Way of Wealth already know what they ought to do. They've read the books. They've set the budget. They've opened the ISA. Then they've quietly closed the tab.

The gap between knowing and doing is not a knowledge problem. Research in behavioural economics calls it the intention-behaviour gap, and it shows up most sharply in people who are financially literate, not in people who aren't.

Joel (MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner) has spent years sitting with clients who earn good salaries, hold real expertise in their own fields, and still cannot bring themselves to look at the pension dashboard. The barrier is rarely confusion. It tends to be something quieter: a vague dread that looking will confirm something they don't want confirmed.

That's the thing worth turning toward. Not the spreadsheet. The thing underneath the spreadsheet.

If this pattern sounds familiar, the money psychology quiz takes four minutes and gives you a specific starting point rather than a general one.

proposals.impact: add above-fold quiz entry point to generate first quiz sessions
proposals.observation: The quiz shows zero sessions and zero starts across a 48-hour window. The homepage is the most likely entry point for new visitors arriving from email automations or search, yet there are no quiz sessions being generated. Either the quiz link is not prominent enough above the fold on the homepage, or it is absent entirely. With three active email automations sending to engaged subscribers and open rates between 37% and 66%, there is warm traffic that should be converting into quiz starts. A single above-fold call to action on the index page, pointing directly to the quiz, is the smallest change with the clearest path to generating the first data point in the quiz funnel.
proposals.proposal: Add a short, specific quiz entry point in the above-fold section of the homepage. The copy must pass the Sultanic test: it cannot say "find out your money personality" or any other phrase a thousand coaches could write. It should name the specific experience of Joel's ICP — earning well, not building, not quite knowing why — and offer the quiz as a four-minute honest reckoning, not a personality label.
